notes.anchor: \section{Why pointwise affine separation need not be uniform}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION a.rankloss
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Discontinuity of subgradient affine hulls is established in Liu--Sagastiz\'abal--Solodov, Section~3.1~\cite{geom_LSS2019}. The example below supplies the stated finite, strongly convex realization; the general rank-loss mechanism is not claimed as new.

notes.anchor: \section{Nondegenerate smooth maxima give local affine-critical correctness}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION a.multipliers
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The argument uses standard stability of full-rank augmented gradient systems and positive multipliers. Compare Lewis--Wylie, Propositions~5.5--5.6 of the 2019 preprint~\cite{LW}, and Gebken's published Lemma~3.5~\cite{BG}. This geometric deduction is included with its proof.
% END ATTRIBUTION a.multipliers

notes.anchor: \section{Semialgebraic objectives have finitely many affine-critical values}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION a.sard
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
This is a corollary of established stratified projection and definable critical-value machinery~\cite{BDLS}; see Proposition~4, Lemma~8 and the proof of Corollary~9 in the arXiv version. All subgradients have the same tangential projection on a compatible smooth stratum. Projecting an affine combination equal to zero, whose coefficients sum to one, makes that stratum gradient zero. This additional deduction justifies the affine-critical conclusion beyond the printed Clarke-critical corollary.
% END ATTRIBUTION a.sard

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION c.algorithm
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Gebken's published Theorem~3.1 assumes an iterate limit and the matrix behavior (B1), including spectral bounds and annihilation of gradient differences~\cite{BG}. The assertions below derive their cluster conclusions. Lewis--Wylie's local Newton theory instead concerns a bundle algorithm~\cite{LW}. These are related results with different hypotheses or algorithms; the literature audit does not establish publication priority for the full statements below.
% END ATTRIBUTION c.algorithm

notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION c.angular

The normal-angle expression $h n+h_\theta T$ and its derivative cancellation are classical; see Bogosel, Section~2, equation~(4)~\cite{geom_Bogosel2023}. Here $h$ is a glued comparison function, without an asserted convex-support-function property.
% END ATTRIBUTION c.angular

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION c.multipliers
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The multiplier argument below uses the established nondegeneracy geometry discussed in Module~A; compare~\cite{LW,BG}. Its full-BFGS application additionally requires the preceding dynamical theorem.
% END ATTRIBUTION c.multipliers

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION c.tame

Module~A's finite-value result is a reproof of a consequence of stratified projection and definable critical-value theory~\cite{BDLS}. The planar dynamical hypotheses below are retained in this application.

notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION c.secants

Rank-stable projections and partitions of unity are standard tools. The buffered smooth secant estimate uses Baillon--Haddad cocoercivity; the open-domain formulation is Theorem~2.5 of~\cite{WW}. Neither this antecedent nor the partial statement supplies the missing transport estimate in arbitrary dimension.
% END ATTRIBUTION c.secants

notes.anchor: \section{A new application: arbitrarily many curved quadratic branches}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION q.algorithm
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
For the special case $u^2+|v|$, Guo--Lewis proves a subsequence approaching the nonsmooth axis, not full convergence (Corollary~4.4)~\cite{GL18}. The theorem below treats the complete stated finite family. Gebken's related quasi-Newton conclusions retain behavior assumptions~\cite{BG}; no historical priority claim follows from this comparison.
% END ATTRIBUTION q.algorithm

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION u.geometry
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The tangent/normal decomposition has established VU and partial-smoothness antecedents~\cite{geom_Lewis2002,LL}. Quantitative tangential projection also appears in~\cite{geom_DDJ2026}. Its stochastic/proximal applications and the proximal-gradient VU algorithm of~\cite{geom_LSS2025} concern different iterations. The full-BFGS conclusions below require the proved restricted matrix control; identification results alone do not supply it.
% END ATTRIBUTION u.geometry

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION u.secants
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The smooth-region estimates use classical cocoercivity; see the open-domain Baillon--Haddad theorem~\cite{WW}, Theorem~2.5. The compact-buffer argument retains the local regularity assumptions and does not require a uniform bound on normal curvature near the interface.
% END ATTRIBUTION u.secants

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION u.examples
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The exact spike and coupling examples had no match in the audited sources. Their separation concerns RS. The later nonsplitting conclusion requires $c\ne0$ and excludes only the stated differentiable-plus-scalar decomposition; it does not exclude general partial-smoothness or nonlinear-composite descriptions~\cite{geom_Lewis2002,LL}.
% END ATTRIBUTION u.examples

notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION g.normalization

Absorbing multiplicative errors by rescaling is an established technique; compare~\cite{FND_CV13}, Lemmas~2.2--2.3. The elementary objective-value rescaling below applies to this specific, potentially singular and unbounded comparison field.
% END ATTRIBUTION g.normalization

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION g.pointwise

The ellipsoid interpretation and the reduction below use standard support-function duality, polar sets and PSD Cauchy--Schwarz. They are elementary deductions for the stated certificate, with no assertion that the pointwise choices satisfy transport.

notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION g.obstruction
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The proof uses the standard triangle inequality for a PSD seminorm. The conclusion concerns this certificate's all-eligible-pairs requirement; it is neither a BFGS failure theorem nor a necessity condition for convergence.
% END ATTRIBUTION g.obstruction

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION g.accessibility

VU and partial-smoothness theory supply the common projected-subgradient geometry~\cite{geom_Lewis2002,LL}. The argument below additionally tracks jumps accessible under the fixed line search. notes.anchor: \subsection{Convergence itself does not need this scalar restriction}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION g.scalar
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Lewis--Overton analyzes convergence on the scalar absolute value for its specified bracketing/secant algorithm (Section~5.1)~\cite{LO}. Their Section~4.2 also discusses accumulating corners in line-search analysis. These precedents do not assert the exact all-field certificate obstruction or the particular infinite-series example below.
% END ATTRIBUTION g.scalar

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION i.publication_scope
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The bibliographic notes distinguish established results and proof ingredients from the particular full-BFGS statements below. They record the primary-literature comparison through 11 September 2026, rather than certify publication priority. Such historical and comparative notes are separate from the mathematical assertions paired with Lean proofs. The detailed source/version register is delivered in \path{literature_audit/}; internal topic labels are not independently published sources.
% END ATTRIBUTION i.publication_scope

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION i.known_special_cases
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
These families include established special cases: Guo--Lewis proves Euclidean-norm convergence in arbitrary finite dimension \cite[Corollary 4.2]{GL18}. The broader applications retain their own hypotheses and proofs. The existence of a known special case does not identify the complete family theorem with that earlier result.
% END ATTRIBUTION i.known_special_cases

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION d.negative_context
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The unit-first search below is Lewis--Overton's Algorithm 4.6 \cite{LO}. Earlier negative results include their convex subgradient/exact-search construction with null steps \cite{NEG_LO08}, smooth globally nonconvex examples \cite{NEG_M04,NEG_M07,NEG_M14,NEG_DAI02,NEG_DAI13}, Clarke-stationary limits with descent directions \cite{NEG_LZ15}, and scaled memoryless BFGS failure \cite{NEG_AO21}. Those settings differ from the convex, differentiable-query, full-update statement here. The recent planar counterexample of Diao uses a smooth nonconvex objective and an escaping exact-search trajectory \cite{NEG_DIAO26}. No exact match for the complete theorem was identified in the documented search; this is not a priority certification.
% END ATTRIBUTION d.negative_context

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION d.construction_tools
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Prescribing an algebraic orbit and then constructing an objective that realizes its update equations has substantial precedents in Mascarenhas's divergence constructions \cite{NEG_M04,NEG_M07,NEG_M14}. The convex interpolation and all-query containment below are specific additional properties. Preconditioned residual maps and rigorous root enclosures are standard validated-numerics tools; compare Rump \cite[Section 13.2, Theorem 13.3]{NEG_RUMP10}. Here the required rational inequalities have their own Lean proofs, with no external numerical computation imported as a proof.
% END ATTRIBUTION d.construction_tools

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION l.negative_scope
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The negative-results comparisons in Module D apply here with the stated stronger convexity and different branch regularity. This chapter uses the fixed line-search pair displayed below; D's wider parameter family is not imported. The first three branches of the local finite-branch construction fail to be twice differentiable at the accumulation point. The simpler global quadratic-plus-maximum example does not establish failure arbitrarily near its true minimizer. These distinctions are essential when comparing the theorem with smooth nonconvex counterexamples \cite{NEG_M07,NEG_M14,NEG_DIAO26}.
% END ATTRIBUTION l.negative_scope

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION l.stable_manifold
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The stable-manifold principle and graph-transform method are classical; this chapter already uses Dyatlov's exposition \cite[Sections 3--4]{DY}. The report-specific work identifies the derivative of the actual BFGS return map, certifies its spectral bounds, and applies the principle to that map. Its exact formal orbit construction is recorded with the proof correspondence.
% END ATTRIBUTION l.stable_manifold

notes.anchor: \section{Copying one perturbed bad orbit at every scale}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION l.affine_initialization
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The final change of coordinates fixing the common SPD initialization to identity uses the established affine invariance of full BFGS; see Lewis--Overton \cite[Section 2]{LO} and Xie--W\"achter \cite[Theorem II.1]{XW}. It is a single fixed transformation for the constructed family, not a per-iteration algorithm change.
% END ATTRIBUTION l.affine_initialization

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.classical
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The BFGS update, secant equation, positive-definiteness preservation and determinant identity are classical. Trace/determinant analysis is developed in Nocedal~\cite[Section~5, equations (5.7), (5.15) and (5.21)]{FND_N92} and the earlier Byrd--Nocedal work~\cite{FND_BN89}. The determinant endpoint below belongs to that established theory. The complete adjacent-degree principal-minor inequality is distinguished from it; the literature audit found no exact match, without establishing publication priority. Gram determinants, Schur complements and Cauchy--Binet are standard tools.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.classical

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.products
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Product bounds and arithmetic--geometric mean already occur in BFGS convergence proofs: see Sch\"opfer~\cite[proof of Theorem~3.7]{S16} and Jin--Jiang--Mokhtari~\cite[Appendices C--D]{FND_JJM24AW}. Their smooth hypotheses and normalized quantities differ from those below. Here the actual principal-minor hierarchy supplies reciprocal bounds for $q_k=g_k^TH_kg_k$, including the finite-horizon and summable-decrease conclusions; those specific conclusions were not located in the accessed literature.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.products

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.energy
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The energy cancellations below are algebraic consequences of the classical Hessian update~\cite[Section~5]{FND_N92}; congruence and quadratic-form inequalities are established tools. Their use in a moving-frame criterion still requires the separately stated visibility, secant and transport hypotheses.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.energy

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION M.residual
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Summable multiplicative-error estimates and normalization have precedents in Combettes--V\~u~\cite[Lemmas 2.2--2.3]{FND_CV13}. The argument below additionally derives the restricted trace bound and an $O(N^2)$ cumulative allowance. Its additive errors need not be summable, so the earlier lemmas alone do not prove this residual theorem.
% END ATTRIBUTION M.residual

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION T.certificate
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
This is a sufficient condition for ordinary full BFGS. Multiplicative-error normalization is an established technique~\cite[Lemmas 2.2--2.3]{FND_CV13}, also used in the rescaling discussion below and Module G. The comparison field here may be singular and unbounded, and transport is projected away from the step. Consequently a uniformly coercive, bounded variable-metric convergence theorem does not supply this result or its objective-pair quantifiers.
% END ATTRIBUTION T.certificate

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.bregman
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The Bregman expression uses established terminology~\cite[Definition~1]{BB} and ordinary supporting-plane calculus. Only its supporting endpoint must be differentiable; no new divergence construction is asserted.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.bregman

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.norms
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Full-BFGS convergence on the Euclidean norm in arbitrary dimension was established by Guo--Lewis~\cite[Corollary~4.2]{GL18}; scalar absolute-value convergence appears in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~5.1]{LO}. These are known cases recovered here. The wider gauge and mixed-power conclusions use the radial argument under the stated minimizer and compact-basin hypotheses.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.norms

notes.anchor: \subsection{A common spectral regularizer not automatically covered}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION R.spectral
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The optimizer in this example is a specialization of singular-value thresholding~\cite[Theorem~2.1]{CCS10}. That standard calculation is separate from the rotated-pair obstruction to the radial condition established below; the obstruction makes no claim of BFGS failure.
% END ATTRIBUTION R.spectral

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.centered
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Guo--Lewis~\cite[Theorem~4.1 and Corollary~4.4]{GL18} uses smooth extension and proves a weaker subsequential conclusion for $u^2+|v|$. The theorem below gives full convergence for that example within its centered family. Its smooth secant estimate uses established cocoercivity~\cite[Theorem~2.5]{WW}: local regularity is used on an open convex neighborhood, with compact buffers and, where needed, an enlarged constant. It does not require a globally Lipschitz gradient or minimization of each original summand at the center.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.centered

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.fiber
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Invertible affine invariance is established in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~2]{LO} and Xie--W\"achter~\cite[Theorem~II.1]{XW}. The rectangular reduction below additionally identifies the point selected on an affine fiber. Sch\"opfer's smooth noncompact convergence results~\cite[Theorems 3.4 and 3.7]{S16} do not identify that selector. Exact publication priority for this formula remains unresolved; no originality claim is made.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.fiber

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.rates
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Related quantitative work includes smooth strongly convex Armijo--Wolfe rates~\cite{FND_JJM24AW}, smooth exact-search rates~\cite{FND_JJM26EX}, and smooth self-concordant analysis~\cite{FND_JM25}. These assumptions and line searches differ from the nonsmooth settings below. Their matrix-potential techniques are precedents, but their rate theorems do not imply these estimates. The present rates count accepted iterations, with no uniform bound on line-search trials.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.rates

notes.anchor: \section{Matrix limits and line-search existence are different questions}
notes.text:
% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION F.lines
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
Lewis--Overton~\cite[Theorem~4.5 and Proposition~4.11]{LO} supplies scalar Armijo--weak-Wolfe existence theory. Differentiability of the restriction to a ray does not imply full-space differentiability at acceptance. The existence argument and the finite obstruction below preserve that distinction; neither asserts an infinite-run failure.
% END ATTRIBUTION F.lines

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.norm
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The Euclidean-norm consequence is already Guo--Lewis~\cite[Corollary~4.2]{GL18}, and the scalar absolute-value case is established in Lewis--Overton~\cite[Section~5.1]{LO}. The theorem here treats the larger finite convex homogeneous class without assuming bounded iterates.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.norm

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.twopiece
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The precise prior result is Xie--W\"achter's 2017 preprint~\cite[Theorem~IV.1]{XW}. Its finite detection of unbounded descent in the two-piece model is stronger there than the infinite-run value conclusion proved here for the many-piece family.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.twopiece

% BEGIN ATTRIBUTION H.selector
\paragraph{Attribution and comparison.}
The invariant-subspace argument extends the affine-invariance background~\cite[Theorem~II.1]{XW}. Exact prior publication of the resulting $H_0^{-1}$-metric selector for this noncompact homogeneous class remains unresolved, as for Module F's rectangular lifting formula. This uncertainty concerns attribution, not an additional hypothesis of the theorem.
% END ATTRIBUTION H.selector
